courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

lectures.title: Syncing the Form to the Template

cues.en: To synchronize this and make sure that our template is connected to this programmatically created form,
we use a bunch of directives which are unlocked by adding the reactive forms module to our ngModule
here.
First of all, we want to use a form wrapper again. So I'll add this form element, the regular form HTML
element around my entire grid that contains all these form inputs. Now on this form wrapper, I will add a
new directive, form group, to which I bind dynamically and this will point at my form property and that
is just that form we're creating programmatically here.
So now, this overall form is synced to that but of course I need to tell Angular which of my programmatically
created controls here belongs to which template control because it does not automatically try
to figure that out
and honestly, it would have a hard time because whilst for us humans it's pretty clear that this is our
title because we have that label here,
it's not really that clear that this input here should hold the value for this title control and it
would be pretty bad if Angular would make such guesses.
So instead, we tell it by adding the form control name directive to that input, without square brackets,
just binding to a string here and that should be the name you chose as a key name here in your form,
so title, description, price, date from and date to. These are the names I chose there and these are the
names I now have to use here,
so I'll bind this to title and this tells Angular that in this form, this input belongs to the title form
control.
Of course I'll do the same for this text area here,
there I'll add form control name and set this equal to description which was the name I chose in TypeScript
and for the price here, it's form control
name price, again using that name I set up there in Typescript.
Now for the dates, it's no different.
Here I add form control name date from and for the second date time, I use form control
name date to
and that is it.
Now we connected the form to the form in Typescript and the result can already be seen if I now go
to onCreateOffer and there, I don't console log this text but instead I can console log this form here.
If we do that, let's wait for that to reload and I click this checkmark, we indeed see the form control,
the form group excuse me and under the controls, we see date from, date to, description and so on and we also
see that in the value object down there,
here we get these same fields.
Now if I clear the console and I enter a title and some description and a price that is 0 to start
with and then I choose a date, let's say here 1st January 2020
and it is available all the way to December 31st 2021,
if I now hit this checkmark,
we see that under value, we can see these values we chose. There also is how we get that date and we also
see that the price is zero but that the overall form is not valid because of that price which is also
marked as red.
If I set this to 100 here, now this looks better and now if I clear the output and submit this
again, we see that overall validity is true and we still see all the values here.
So that is how we can now work with this form,
we don't need to pass it as an argument in our submit function because it already is in the Typescript
code.
